papers.title: mTOR signalling, not clock gene rhythms, organises daily physiology
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that mTOR is a major clock output pathway required for most daily variation in mammalian physiology, with PERIOD2 interacting directly with mTORC1. Acute mTOR inhibition abolishes functional rhythms in cells and most daily liver physiology, while preserving sleep/wake cycles, and shows evolutionary conservation as a circadian effector across species.

papers.title: Diphenhydramine disrupts sleep architecture in 5XFAD Alzheimer's disease model and wild-type mice.
papers.journal: Neurobiology of sleep and circadian rhythms
papers.summary: Chronic diphenhydramine treatment fragmented NREM2 sleep and disrupted sleep architecture in both 5XFAD and wild-type female mice, without rescuing Alzheimer's-related sleep deficits.

papers.title: Characterization of Sleep, Spectral, and Epileptiform Activity in Individuals Aged 8-27 Years with SYNGAP1-Related Disorder Using an at-Home Dry EEG Headband
papers.summary: Using an at-home dry-electrode EEG headband in a decentralized protocol, the study collected 180 recordings from 23 participants with SYNGAP1-related disorder, showing increased wake after sleep onset, reduced sleep efficiency, altered sleep-stage distribution, and interictal epileptiform discharges in 22 of 23 participants. It also reproduced awake spectral abnormalities and revealed sleep-stage-dependent spectral biomarker dynamics.

papers.title: Sleep neurophysiology as a biological correlate of infant temperament.
papers.summary: In 6-month-old infants, frontal slow-wave activity asymmetry and prefrontal theta power during sleep correlated with orienting/regulatory capacity and negative affectivity, respectively, linking sleep neurophysiology to temperament.

papers.title: Detection of Spreading Depolarization with Noninvasive Electroencephalography
papers.summary: Developed and validated WAVEFRONT, a noninvasive scalp EEG biomarker of spreading depolarization based on delta-band spatiotemporal propagation, trained against concurrent invasive subdural ECoG in TBI, SAH, and stroke patients. Cross-validated true positive rate was 97.3±1% with 6.0±0.5% false positives, detection duration correlated with ECoG SD counts (R²=0.7411), and in the independent I-CARE cardiac arrest cohort biomarker burden on day 3 was higher in patients with poor neurological outcome (p=0.007).

papers.title: Improved motor learning in adenosine A1 receptor knockout mice.
papers.summary: Compared motor skill learning on an accelerating rotarod between adenosine A1 receptor knockout and wild-type mice, finding knockout mice learned faster and reached better Day 5 performance, whereas wild-type mice showed superior one-week retention. Older animals showed greater learning gains and retention, with no sex differences and no relation of individual variability to baseline activity or anxiety.

papers.title: Motor memory consolidation during sleep after stroke: the rehabilitation timing hypothesis.
papers.summary: Reviews mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical evidence for a rehabilitation timing hypothesis in which motor therapy scheduled near sleep enhances sleep-dependent motor memory consolidation after stroke. Identifies sleep spindles nested in NREM slow oscillations as a principal substrate disrupted by stroke, and concludes that direct stroke evidence is lacking and trials testing therapy timing as an independent variable are needed.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Slow Wave Sleep Detection from Single-Lead EEG in Pediatric Congenital Heart Disease Recovery.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Developed PCPS-SleepNet, a deep learning framework for cross-domain slow-wave sleep detection from single-lead EEG in pediatric congenital heart disease recovery, achieving 75.65% accuracy and 87.89% AUPRC for SWS detection.

papers.title: Circadian-melatonin signaling in general anesthesia: molecular mechanisms and perioperative implications.
papers.summary: Reviews how anesthetic agents, surgical stress, and the perioperative environment interact with suprachiasmatic, peripheral clock, and pineal melatonin signaling, including proposed clock-repression and metabolic mechanisms largely unconfirmed in humans. Concludes preoperative melatonin anxiolysis is the best-supported indication, while evidence for postoperative sleep, analgesia, delirium prevention, and organ protection remains heterogeneous and of low certainty.

papers.title: Sequential Associations of Sleep Architecture, Nocturnal Oxygenation, and Respiratory Disturbance With a Composite PSG-Derived Rhythm-Event Index.
papers.summary: In 41 patients undergoing polysomnography, a sequential negative binomial regression model found that only higher sleep efficiency was robustly associated with lower composite PSG-derived rhythm-event rate (IRR = 0.946 per percentage point, 95% CI 0.921-0.972), while AHI and other respiratory indices were not independently associated. The authors note the exploratory and hypothesis-generating nature of these findings.

papers.title: Sigma-1 receptor alleviates postoperative cognitive dysfunction exacerbated by preoperative acute sleep deprivation in mice via modulating the Keap1/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: In a mouse model combining preoperative acute sleep deprivation with exploratory laparotomy, sigma-1 receptor agonism with PRE-084 reversed postoperative cognitive deficits, suppressed neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, and promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation via sigma-1R association with Keap1, while antagonist BD-1047 worsened injury and Nrf2 inhibition blocked protection.

papers.title: A representation-level wavelet-EMD fusion framework for spectral analysis and detection of epileptiform patterns in pediatric EEG: computational validation with a roadmap for external benchmarking.
papers.summary: Proposed a representation-level wavelet-EMD fusion framework for pediatric epileptiform EEG analysis, achieving 94.6% accuracy on synthetic data and 86.7% accuracy on CHB-MIT external validation.

papers.title: Combined vitamins C and E attenuate memory impairment and hippocampal damage in diabetic sleep-deprived mice: behavioral and molecular insights.
papers.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
papers.summary: Combined vitamin C and E treatment attenuated memory impairment and hippocampal damage in diabetic sleep-deprived mice, with increased BDNF, Nrf2, and HO-1 and reduced iNOS, TNF-α, and IL-1β expression.

papers.title: Sleep Strategies and Performance Outcomes in Ultramarathon Runners: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review examined associations between pre-race and intra-race sleep strategies and physical and cognitive performance in ultramarathon runners, including nine studies with 2262 participants. Greater pre-race sleep duration, including sleep extension, was associated with faster finish times, while greater intra-race sleep duration was consistently associated with longer finish times.

papers.title: Interactions between sleep parameters and heart rate variability in temporomandibular disorders.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 93 patients with temporomandibular disorders (TMD) using video-polysomnography and 24-hour ECG, high TMD-related pain intensity was associated with lower sleep efficiency (87.7% vs 90.8%) and lower mean oxygen saturation during sleep (94.7% vs 95.2%), while heart rate variability parameters were similar between pain groups. Women reported higher total pain scores but showed lower sympathetic activation (higher pNN50 and RMSSD, lower VLF and LF/HF ratio) than men.

papers.title: The toll of an early bell? School start time and adolescent sleep quality in Flanders, Belgium
papers.summary: Using 2022 Flemish HBSC data from 12,329 secondary-school adolescents across 94 schools and both linear regression and debiased machine learning, this study found no clinically meaningful effect of school start times on sleep duration or sleep quality; a 10-minute delay was associated with non-significant changes in sleep quality (0.01 points on a 1-5 scale) and school-day sleep duration (3.5 minutes).

papers.title: Seasonal Variation in Mood and Associated Patterns of Sleep, Activity, Circadian Rhythms and Light.
papers.summary: In 733 wrist-actigraphy observation periods from 422 young Australians with emerging mood disorders, depressive and negative symptoms peaked in winter while manic symptoms peaked in autumn. Winter increases in negative symptoms were indirectly associated with an 'extended sleep with phase-delayed activity' profile and a constrained moderate-to-bright indoor light exposure pattern, and winter depressive symptoms with lower physical activity.

papers.title: Gene-by-Sleep Duration Interaction for Glycemic Traits in More Than 480,000 Individuals.
papers.summary: A large-scale gene-by-sleep-duration interaction analysis in more than 480,000 individuals identified 16 loci (11 novel) interacting with short or long sleep duration to influence HbA1c, fasting glucose, or fasting insulin, with short- and long-sleep loci being nonoverlapping. Implicated mechanisms included copper regulation for long-sleep loci and diacylglycerol regulation for short-sleep loci, suggesting targets relevant to type 2 diabetes therapeutic design.

papers.title: Federated Spiking GANs with Rényi Differential Privacy for privacy-preserving synthetic EEG generation in brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: The authors developed a federated spiking GAN framework combining an SNN-based generator, temporally correlated noise, an ANN-based discriminator, and Rényi differential privacy for generating privacy-preserving synthetic EEG data for brain-computer interfaces. Benchmarked against RDP-TimeGAN, RDP-CRNN-GAN, RDP-RCGAN, and RDP-Clare-GAN, the approach reportedly preserved temporal features and downstream utility while maintaining privacy.

papers.title: EEG-Based Cognitive Overload-Driven Adaptive Training for Enhancing Performance Under Simulated High-Stress Space Operation Tasks.
papers.summary: Developed an EEG-based cognitive overload-driven adaptive training system combining hybrid feature selection, NFDTW feature alignment, and a dual-factor task regulation strategy. Online overload detection reached 92.07% and 84.67% accuracy on two datasets, and the adaptive group showed significantly improved task performance and stress/anxiety scores in a VR robotic arm docking task.

papers.title: Who's Been Sleeping in My Bedroom? Associations Between Co-Sleeping with Dogs, Cats, or Children and Sleep and Cardiorespiratory Physiology Among WHOOP Users.
papers.summary: Analyzed 1,649,083 person-days from 11,733 WHOOP wearable users to test within-person associations between co-sleeping with dogs, cats, or children and sleep and cardiorespiratory physiology. Co-sleeping was associated with small but significant changes, including lower resting heart rate (0.8-1.1 beats/min), higher heart rate variability (1.41-1.95 ms), longer sleep duration but more disturbances, and higher next-day activity after dog or cat co-sleeping, with all effect sizes small.

papers.title: Subtle Alterations of Tidal Breathing Variables in Healthy Late Preterm Neonates at Term-Equivalent Age.
papers.summary: Prospective cross-sectional study compared tidal breathing variables in 60 healthy late-preterm and 60 term neonates at term-equivalent age. Late-preterm neonates had modestly lower tPTEF/tE (27.4% vs. 31.2%) and VPTEF/VE, and each additional week of gestational age was associated with a 1.18-percentage-point increase in tPTEF/tE.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture improves endometrial receptivity and pregnancy outcomes in controlled ovarian hyperstimulation rats by restoring Per2 circadian rhythm.
papers.summary: In a controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) rat model with Per2-/- mouse validation, electroacupuncture corrected abnormal progesterone levels, restored Per2 circadian rhythm parameters, upregulated Vegf and integrin αvβ3, improved pinopode development, and significantly increased pregnancy rate. The weakened electroacupuncture effect in Per2-/- mice suggests Per2 may mediate its effects on endometrial receptivity.

papers.title: The moderating role of anger rumination and self-control in the day-to-day associations between irritability and sleep in male adolescents: An exploratory experience sampling method study.
papers.summary: A 9-day experience sampling study in 56 male adolescents found that poorer sleep quality predicted higher next-day irritability, and that daily anger rumination and self-control directly predicted next-day irritability, with sleep-irritability associations moderated by between-person rumination and self-control; lower irritability also predicted better subsequent sleep quality.

papers.title: Association Between Circadian Rhythm Sleep Disorder and Noninfectious Uveitis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort study in the TriNetX network comparing 47,323 adults with circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder to 22,241 polysomnography controls, finding CRSD independently associated with increased incident noninfectious uveitis (anterior aHR 1.70; composite aHR 1.84). Control outcomes behaved as expected, supporting a potential role for circadian dysregulation in ocular inflammatory disease.

papers.title: Circadian clock adjusted classes improve sleep, circadian health, and academic performance in medical freshmen.
papers.summary: Randomized 71 first-year medical students with high social jetlag to a later-start (classes ≥10:00) or standard 8:00 schedule and found that later circadian temperature phase predicted lower exam scores, while the later-start group performed similarly to early-phase students and showed greater rest-activity and blue-light stability and longer sleep.

papers.title: Assessment of the duration of continuous EEG monitoring in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
papers.summary: Retrospective comparison of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage patients receiving a standard 6-7 day versus longer continuous EEG monitoring protocol, finding no difference in detection of worsening EEG activity, vasospasm, or delayed cerebral ischemia. Longer monitoring was independently associated with nearly doubled ICU and hospital length of stay but not with vasospasm, DCI, or 6-month functional outcome.

papers.title: Indoor NO2, temperature, and humidity in relation to maternal stress, sleep, and cognitive performance during pregnancy.
papers.summary: In 906 pregnant participants from the BiSC cohort with objectively measured indoor exposures, higher indoor NO2 was associated with higher perceived stress but not with sleep quality or cognitive performance, while indoor temperature and relative humidity showed no associations with any outcome.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG functional connectivity changes following memantine administration in children with autism spectrum disorder: an exploratory pre-post study.
papers.summary: In 22 preschool children with autism spectrum disorder, one month of memantine treatment was associated with heterogeneous changes in resting-state EEG functional connectivity: 64% showed increased network integration and 36% decreased connectivity, with spatial network reorganization involving localized suppression in fronto-central and left occipital regions and enhanced long-range coupling in right parietal and left temporal regions.

papers.title: Network analysis of frailty, sleep quality, and life satisfaction in older patients: a cross-sectional study stratified by chronic disease burden.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional network analysis of 1,107 older patients (97.4% with multimorbidity), life satisfaction nodes showed high strength and bridge centrality, sleep-related nodes (sleep latency, sleeping medication use, daytime dysfunction) were prominent in centrality indices, and frailty nodes connected to life satisfaction mainly through negative edges; negative cross-community connections appeared more pronounced in those with ≥5 chronic diseases, though between-group differences were descriptive.

papers.title: Case Report: Smith-Magenis syndrome with bilateral high-grade vesicoureteral reflux, hypothyroidism, and seizure in infancy.
papers.summary: A 9-month-old boy with recurrent febrile urinary tract infection, bilateral high-grade vesicoureteral reflux, hypothyroidism, global developmental delay, and dysmorphic features was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis syndrome via trio whole-exome sequencing identifying a de novo 3.63-Mb 17p11.2 deletion encompassing RAI1; management included antibiotics, levothyroxine, and antibiotic prophylaxis, with improved renal indices and no recurrent urinary tract infection at follow-up.

papers.title: When a Seizure Reveals More Than a Hemorrhage: When to Suspect Cerebral Cavernous Malformations.
papers.summary: Case report of a 33-year-old woman with generalized tonic-clonic seizures after sleep deprivation whose CT suggested left frontal hemorrhage but MRI revealed two left frontal Zabramski type II cerebral cavernous malformations. The case illustrates CT limitations and the value of MRI for detecting multiple cavernomas, raising suspicion for familial CCM and supporting individualized management.

papers.title: The role and mechanism of endothelial cell-specific molecule-1 in respiratory diseases.
papers.summary: Review of endothelial cell-specific molecule-1 (ESM1/endocan), a pulmonary endothelial proteoglycan with dual inflammatory regulation, summarizing its involvement in signaling pathways (EGFR, HGF/c-MET, VEGF-A, mTOR, PI3K/AKT) and in respiratory diseases including lung cancer, OSAHS, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and ALI/ARDS. It proposes ESM1 as a potential therapeutic target while noting unclear roles in COPD, asthma, and pneumonia.

papers.title: Association between lactic dehydrogenase-to-albumin ratio and all-cause mortality in critical obstructive sleep apnea patients: a retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC-IV database.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 1,118 critically ill obstructive sleep apnea patients from MIMIC-IV, higher lactate dehydrogenase-to-albumin ratio (LDAR) was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality at 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, and 1 year, with a positive linear relationship and a 139.8% higher 90-day mortality risk in the highest versus lowest LDAR quartile.

papers.title: A systematic review of economic evaluations of strategies to diagnose obstructive sleep apnoea in adults.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 29 economic evaluations of diagnostic strategies for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea found substantial methodological heterogeneity in diagnostic thresholds, model structures, and assumptions about CPAP adherence, with only four studies using home respiratory polygraphy as a comparator, limiting applicability to the UK setting and leaving the true cost-effectiveness of contemporary diagnostic pathways uncertain.

papers.title: Real-Time Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Monitoring With Digital Triage and Care-Team Integration in Early Breast Cancer: ENABLE Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In the ENABLE multicenter open-label RCT, adding weekly ePRO screening with rule-based digital triage and care-team escalation to app-based support in early breast cancer produced domain-specific, sub-minimally-important differences at end of treatment versus an active digital comparator: reduced fatigue (-3.90 T-score points), social participation improvement (+2.84), and reduced anxiety (-2.10), with no intervention-related harms; 76.6% of monitored patients triggered at least one alert.

papers.title: Participation in an integrated telemedicine and psychological counseling program and psychological outcomes in patients with HCC: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.summary: In a multicenter retrospective cohort of 349 hepatocellular carcinoma patients, moderate and high cumulative participation in an integrated telemedicine and psychological counseling program was associated with lower PHQ-9 depression scores (β = -2.64 and -3.73) and other favorable psychological outcomes (sleep, distress, anxiety) but with poorer FACT-Hep disease-specific quality of life, and the authors noted clinical significance remains uncertain due to selection and confounding.

papers.title: Cryptococcal meningitis-associated cerebrovascular injury presenting with sequential multifocal cerebral infarctions and prominent autonomic dysfunction in a non-HIV patient: a case report and focused literature review.
papers.summary: Reports a 66-year-old non-HIV man with cryptococcal meningitis initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke, who developed sequential multifocal infarctions (brainstem, cerebellar vermis, corpus callosum, thalamus) with prominent autonomic dysfunction and improved after serial lumbar punctures and amphotericin B/fluconazole. A focused literature review contextualizes CM-associated cerebral infarction in apparently immunocompetent patients, noting poorly documented sequential multi-territory infarctions with progressive autonomic syndrome.

papers.title: Mishel theory-based perioperative nursing after trabeculectomy for primary glaucoma: effects on illness uncertainty, self-management, and quality of life.
papers.summary: Single-center randomized controlled trial (n=198) testing Mishel Uncertainty in Illness Theory-based perioperative nursing versus routine care in primary glaucoma patients undergoing trabeculectomy. The intervention group showed lower illness uncertainty at 1 and 3 months (difference -8.13 points) and improved self-management, medication adherence, and vision-related quality of life, with no significant differences in short-term intraocular pressure, visual acuity, or complications.

papers.title: The impact of menstruation-related symptoms on women's quality of life, work productivity, and economic burden: a structured narrative review.
papers.summary: Structured narrative review of 86 studies (2014-2025) examining how dysmenorrhoea, PMS/PMDD, and HMB/AUB affect quality of life, work productivity, and economic burden. Menstruation-related disorders were consistently associated with reduced health-related QOL and productivity loss driven predominantly by presenteeism rather than absenteeism, with psychological distress as a key contributor.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
